evidence: Project uses Django framework with distinct apps (cmdb, system, monitor, oauth, work, information) under drf_admin/apps/, indicating logical separation of domain concerns
Each app follows Django conventions (models, views, serializers, urls, admin, migrations, signals), supporting cohesive modular organization
No inter-process communication mechanisms (e.g., message queues between services, REST/gRPC endpoints between separate processes) — all modules reside in the same codebase and deploy as one unit
Shared infrastructure (Redis, Celery) is used for cross-cutting concerns (caching, background tasks), not inter-service communication
Centralized routing via drf_admin/urls.py, with each app mounting its own URLs
Shared utilities, permissions, and models across apps (e.g., drf_admin/common/, utils/), indicating high cohesion within the monolith and low coupling to external services
No evidence of process boundaries or service discovery; all services are part of one Django project root
risks: Monolithic scaling limitations — difficulty scaling individual components independently
Risk of tight coupling over time if module boundaries are not enforced (e.g., cross-app model imports)
Deployment complexity increases as project grows — full rebuild/deploy needed for any change
Shared state (e.g., Redis, DB) across modules may lead to contention or unintended dependencies
